biography: Alexandre Finardi's journey began on the dusty karting tracks of Ribeirão Preto, Brazil, inhaling the fumes of two-strokes and dreaming of Interlagos. His father, a mechanic with a passion for speed, nurtured his talent, sacrificing weekends to hone Alexandre's skills. A defining moment came at the 2008 Brazilian Karting Championship where, despite a mechanical failure in the final lap, Alexandre pushed his kart across the finish line, securing a hard-fought third place and earning the respect of his peers. This determination caught the eye of Power Imports, who signed him to their touring car team. After a promising start in domestic racing series, Alexandre transitioned to prototype racing, joining MetalMoro MRX Duratec Turbo P3. Now at 35, while his raw speed may be diminishing, his experience and tactical acumen are invaluable assets, even as he faces mounting pressure from younger, hungrier drivers.
drivingStyle: Finardi is a master of consistency, prioritizing smooth lines and calculated risks over outright aggression. He's known for his exceptional tire management, often nursing his rubber to gain an advantage in the later stages of a race. In qualifying, he adopts a methodical approach, building speed gradually throughout the session, rather than going for a 'hero lap' early on. He rarely cracks under pressure, maintaining a calm demeanor even in the most chaotic situations, a trait that has earned him the reputation of a reliable teammate.

rivalries.name: Ricardo Viana
rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their karting days. Viana's aggressive style often clashed with Finardi's calculated approach, leading to numerous on-track incidents.

rivalries.name: Isabela Monteiro
rivalries.reason: Monteiro, a rising star, consistently challenges Finardi's position in the MetalMoro team, creating internal pressure and fueling fierce competition for race victories.

rivalries.name: Kenji Tanaka
rivalries.reason: They battled wheel-to-wheel during the 2022 Brazilian Endurance Championship, resulting in a controversial collision that cost both drivers valuable points and ignited a simmering feud.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of socks gifted to him by his grandmother before every race.
Listens to a specific bossa nova playlist an hour before getting into the car to calm his nerves.
Refuses to drink any beverage with ice on race day, believing it affects his reaction time.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about understanding the dance between man and machine, and knowing when to lead and when to follow."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 Brazilian Touring Car Championship after a season-long battle with Ricardo Viana, securing the title with a masterful drive in the final race at Interlagos.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2021 6 Hours of Goiânia with only 30 minutes remaining, costing MetalMoro a guaranteed victory and damaging his reputation within the team.
